Rule.description: echo is a network service that responds to clients with the data sent to it by the client. This service is intended for debugging and testing purposes. It is recommended that this service be disabled.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Disabling this service will reduce the remote attack surface of the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Comment out or remove any lines starting with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">echo</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disable = yes</xhtml:span> on all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">echo</xhtml:span> services in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.1.5 Ensure time services are not enabled
Rule.description: time is a network service that responds with the server's current date and time as a 32 bit integer. This service is intended for debugging and testing purposes. It is recommended that this service be disabled.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Disabling this service will reduce the remote attack surface of the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Comment out or remove any lines starting with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">time</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disable = yes</xhtml:span> on all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">time</xhtml:span> services in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.1.6 Ensure rsh server is not enabled
Rule.description: The Berkeley rsh-server (rsh, rlogin, rexec) package contains legacy services that exchange credentials in clear-text.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">These legacy services contain numerous security exposures and have been replaced with the more secure SSH package.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Comment out or remove any lines starting with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shell</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">login</xhtml:span> , or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disable = yes</xhtml:span> on all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsh</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rlogin</xhtml:span> , and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rexec</xhtml:span> services in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.1.7 Ensure talk server is not enabled
Rule.description: The talk software makes it possible for users to send and receive messages across systems through a terminal session. The talk client (allows initiate of talk sessions) is installed by default.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The software presents a security risk as it uses unencrypted protocols for communication.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Comment out or remove any lines starting with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">talk</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ntalk</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disable = yes</xhtml:span> on all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">talk</xhtml:span> services in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.1.8 Ensure telnet server is not enabled
Rule.description: The telnet-server package contains the telnet daemon, which accepts connections from users from other systems via the telnet protocol.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">telnet </xhtml:span> protocol is insecure and unencrypted. The use of an unencrypted transmission medium could allow a user with access to sniff network traffic the ability to steal credentials. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh </xhtml:span> package provides an encrypted session and stronger security. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Comment out or remove any lines starting with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">telnet</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disable = yes</xhtml:span> on all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">telnet</xhtml:span> services in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.1.9 Ensure tftp server is not enabled
Rule.description: Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) is a simple file transfer protocol, typically used to automatically transfer configuration or boot machines from a boot server. The packages tftp and atftp are both used to define and support a TFTP server.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">TFTP does not support authentication nor does it ensure the confidentiality or integrity of data. It is recommended that TFTP be removed, unless there is a specific need for TFTP. In that case, extreme caution must be used when configuring the services.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Comment out or remove any lines starting with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftp</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/inetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disable = yes</xhtml:span> on all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftp</xhtml:span> services in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/xinetd.d/*</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.1.10 Ensure xinetd is not enabled
Rule.description: The eXtended InterNET Daemon (xinetd) is an open source super daemon that replaced the original inetd daemon. The xinetd daemon listens for well known services and dispatches the appropriate daemon to properly respond to service requests.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> If there are no <xhtml:span class="inline_block">xinetd </xhtml:span> services required, it is recommended that the daemon be disabled. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">xinetd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable xinetd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 2.2. Special Purpose Services
Group.description: This section describes services that are installed on systems that specifically need to run these services. If any of these services are not required, it is recommended that they be disabled or deleted from the system to reduce the potential attack surface.

Group.title: 2.2.1. Time Synchronization
Group.description: It is recommended that physical systems and virtual guests lacking direct access to the physical host's clock be configured to synchronize their time using a service such as NTP or chrony.

Rule.title: 2.2.1.1 Ensure time synchronization is in use
Rule.description: System time should be synchronized between all systems in an environment. This is typically done by establishing an authoritative time server or set of servers and having all systems synchronize their clocks to them.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Time synchronization is important to support time sensitive security mechanisms like Kerberos and also ensures log files have consistent time records across the enterprise, which aids in forensic investigations.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>On physical systems or virtual systems where host based time synchronization is not available install NTP or chrony using one of the following commands:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # apt-get install ntp <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # apt-get install chrony </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>On virtual systems where host based time synchronization is available consult your virtualization software documentation and setup host based synchronization.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.1.2 Ensure ntp is configured
Rule.description:
ntp is a daemon which implements the Network Time Protocol (NTP). It is designed to synchronize system clocks across a variety of systems and use a source that is highly accurate. More information on NTP can be found at http://www.ntp.org . ntp can be configured to be a client and/or a server.
This recommendation only applies if ntp is in use on the system.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If ntp is in use on the system proper configuration is vital to ensuring time synchronization is working properly.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add or edit restrict lines in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ntp.conf</xhtml:span> to match the following: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> restrict -4 default kod nomodify notrap nopeer noquery <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> restrict -6 default kod nomodify notrap nopeer noquery </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Add or edit server lines to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ntp.conf</xhtml:span> as appropriate: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> server <xhtml:em><remote-server></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Configure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ntp</xhtml:span> to run as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ntp</xhtml:span> user by adding or editing the following file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/init.d/ntp</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">RUNASUSER=ntp</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.1.3 Ensure chrony is configured
Rule.description:
chrony is a daemon which implements the Network Time Protocol (NTP) is designed to synchronize system clocks across a variety of systems and use a source that is highly accurate. More information on chrony can be found at http://chrony.tuxfamily.org/
. chrony can be configured to be a client and/or a server.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If chrony is in use on the system proper configuration is vital to ensuring time synchronization is working properly.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">This recommendation only applies if chrony is in use on the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add or edit server lines to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/chrony/chrony.conf</xhtml:span> as appropriate: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> server <xhtml:em><remote-server></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Configure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> to run as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> user by configuring the appropriate startup script for your distribution. Startup scripts are typically stored in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/init.d</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.3 Ensure Avahi Server is not enabled
Rule.description: Avahi is a free zeroconf implementation, including a system for multicast DNS/DNS-SD service discovery. Avahi allows programs to publish and discover services and hosts running on a local network with no specific configuration. For example, a user can plug a computer into a network and Avahi automatically finds printers to print to, files to look at and people to talk to, as well as network services running on the machine.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Automatic discovery of network services is not normally required for system functionality. It is recommended to disable the service to reduce the potential attach surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">avahi-daemon</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable avahi-daemon</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.4 Ensure CUPS is not enabled
Rule.description: The Common Unix Print System (CUPS) provides the ability to print to both local and network printers. A system running CUPS can also accept print jobs from remote systems and print them to local printers. It also provides a web based remote administration capability.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the system does not need to print jobs or accept print jobs from other systems, it is recommended that CUPS be disabled to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cups</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable cups</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Disabling CUPS will prevent printing from the system, a common task for workstation systems.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.5 Ensure DHCP Server is not enabled
Rule.description: The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is a service that allows machines to be dynamically assigned IP addresses.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Unless a system is specifically set up to act as a DHCP server, it is recommended that this service be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to disable dhcpd:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # systemctl disable isc-dhcp-server <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # systemctl disable isc-dhcp-server6 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.6 Ensure LDAP server is not enabled
Rule.description: The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) was introduced as a replacement for NIS/YP. It is a service that provides a method for looking up information from a central database.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the system will not need to act as an LDAP server, it is recommended that the software be disabled to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">slapd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable slapd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.7 Ensure NFS and RPC are not enabled
Rule.description: The Network File System (NFS) is one of the first and most widely distributed file systems in the UNIX environment. It provides the ability for systems to mount file systems of other servers through the network.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the system does not export NFS shares or act as an NFS client, it is recommended that these services be disabled to reduce remote attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nfs</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rpcbind</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # systemctl disable nfs-kernel-server <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # systemctl disable rpcbind </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.8 Ensure DNS Server is not enabled
Rule.description: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a hierarchical naming system that maps names to IP addresses for computers, services and other resources connected to a network.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Unless a system is specifically designated to act as a DNS server, it is recommended that the package be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">named</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable bind9</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.9 Ensure FTP Server is not enabled
Rule.description: The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) provides networked computers with the ability to transfer files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">FTP does not protect the confidentiality of data or authentication credentials. It is recommended sftp be used if file transfer is required. Unless there is a need to run the system as a FTP server (for example, to allow anonymous downloads), it is recommended that the package be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">vsftpd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable vsftpd </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.10 Ensure HTTP server is not enabled
Rule.description: HTTP or web servers provide the ability to host web site content.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Unless there is a need to run the system as a web server, it is recommended that the package be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">apache2</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable apache2</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.11 Ensure IMAP and POP3 server is not enabled
Rule.description: dovecot is an open source IMAP and POP3 server for Linux based systems.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Unless POP3 and/or IMAP servers are to be provided by this system, it is recommended that the service be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dovecot</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable dovecot</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.12 Ensure Samba is not enabled
Rule.description: The Samba daemon allows system administrators to configure their Linux systems to share file systems and directories with Windows desktops. Samba will advertise the file systems and directories via the Small Message Block (SMB) protocol. Windows desktop users will be able to mount these directories and file systems as letter drives on their systems.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If there is no need to mount directories and file systems to Windows systems, then this service can be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">smbd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable smbd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.13 Ensure HTTP Proxy Server is not enabled
Rule.description: Squid is a standard proxy server used in many distributions and environments.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If there is no need for a proxy server, it is recommended that the squid proxy be deleted to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">squid</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable squid</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.14 Ensure SNMP Server is not enabled
Rule.description: The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) server is used to listen for SNMP commands from an SNMP management system, execute the commands or collect the information and then send results back to the requesting system.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The SNMP server communicates using SNMP v1, which transmits data in the clear and does not require authentication to execute commands. Unless absolutely necessary, it is recommended that the SNMP service not be used.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">snmpd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable snmpd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.15 Ensure mail transfer agent is configured for local-only mode
Rule.description: Mail Transfer Agents (MTA), such as sendmail and Postfix, are used to listen for incoming mail and transfer the messages to the appropriate user or mail server. If the system is not intended to be a mail server, it is recommended that the MTA be configured to only process local mail.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The software for all Mail Transfer Agents is complex and most have a long history of security issues. While it is important to ensure that the system can process local mail messages, it is not necessary to have the MTA's daemon listening on a port unless the server is intended to be a mail server that receives and processes mail from other systems.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/postfix/main.cf </xhtml:span> and add the following line to the RECEIVING MAIL section. If the line already exists, change it to look like the line below: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">inet_interfaces = localhost</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Restart postfix:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># service postfix restart</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.16 Ensure rsync service is not enabled
Rule.description: The rsyncd service can be used to synchronize files between systems over network links.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyncd</xhtml:span> service presents a security risk as it uses unencrypted protocols for communication. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsync</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable rsync</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.2.17 Ensure NIS Server is not enabled
Rule.description: The Network Information Service (NIS) (formally known as Yellow Pages) is a client-server directory service protocol for distributing system configuration files. The NIS server is a collection of programs that allow for the distribution of configuration files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The NIS service is inherently an insecure system that has been vulnerable to DOS attacks, buffer overflows and has poor authentication for querying NIS maps. NIS generally been replaced by such protocols as Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). It is recommended that the service be disabled and other, more secure services be used</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to disable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nis</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl disable nis</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 2.3. Service Clients
Group.description:
A number of insecure services exist. While disabling the servers prevents a local attack against these services, it is advised to remove their clients unless they are required.
Note : This should not be considered a comprehensive list of insecure service clients. You may wish to consider additions to those listed here for your environment.

Rule.title: 2.3.1 Ensure NIS Client is not installed
Rule.description: The Network Information Service (NIS), formerly known as Yellow Pages, is a client-server directory service protocol used to distribute system configuration files. The NIS client (ypbind) was used to bind a machine to an NIS server and receive the distributed configuration files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The NIS service is inherently an insecure system that has been vulnerable to DOS attacks, buffer overflows and has poor authentication for querying NIS maps. NIS generally has been replaced by such protocols as Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). It is recommended that the service be removed.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to uninstall <xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span>nis</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">apt-get remove nis</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many insecure service clients are used as troubleshooting tools and in testing environments. Uninstalling them can inhibit capability to test and troubleshoot. If they are required it is advisable to remove the clients after use to prevent accidental or intentional misuse.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.3.2 Ensure rsh client is not installed
Rule.description: The rsh package contains the client commands for the rsh services.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> These legacy clients contain numerous security exposures and have been replaced with the more secure SSH package. Even if the server is removed, it is best to ensure the clients are also removed to prevent users from inadvertently attempting to use these commands and therefore exposing their credentials. Note that removing the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsh </xhtml:span> package removes the clients for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsh</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rcp </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rlogin</xhtml:span> . </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to uninstall <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsh</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">apt-get remove rsh-client rsh-redone-client</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many insecure service clients are used as troubleshooting tools and in testing environments. Uninstalling them can inhibit capability to test and troubleshoot. If they are required it is advisable to remove the clients after use to prevent accidental or intentional misuse.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.3.3 Ensure talk client is not installed
Rule.description: The talk software makes it possible for users to send and receive messages across systems through a terminal session. The talk client, which allows initialization of talk sessions, is installed by default.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The software presents a security risk as it uses unencrypted protocols for communication.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to uninstall <xhtml:span class="inline_block">talk</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">apt-get remove talk</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many insecure service clients are used as troubleshooting tools and in testing environments. Uninstalling them can inhibit capability to test and troubleshoot. If they are required it is advisable to remove the clients after use to prevent accidental or intentional misuse.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.3.4 Ensure telnet client is not installed
Rule.description: The telnet package contains the telnet client, which allows users to start connections to other systems via the telnet protocol.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">telnet </xhtml:span> protocol is insecure and unencrypted. The use of an unencrypted transmission medium could allow an unauthorized user to steal credentials. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh </xhtml:span> package provides an encrypted session and stronger security and is included in most Linux distributions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to uninstall <xhtml:span class="inline_block">telnet</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt-get remove telnet</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many insecure service clients are used as troubleshooting tools and in testing environments. Uninstalling them can inhibit capability to test and troubleshoot. If they are required it is advisable to remove the clients after use to prevent accidental or intentional misuse.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 2.3.5 Ensure LDAP client is not installed
Rule.description: The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) was introduced as a replacement for NIS/YP. It is a service that provides a method for looking up information from a central database.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the system will not need to act as an LDAP client, it is recommended that the software be removed to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Uninstall <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ldap-utils</xhtml:span> using the appropriate package manager or manual installation: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt-get remove ldap-utils</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Removing the LDAP client will prevent or inhibit using LDAP for authentication in your environment.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 3. Network Configuration
Group.description: This section provides guidance on for securing the network configuration of the system through kernel parameters, access list control, and firewall settings.

Group.title: 3.1. Network Parameters (Host Only)
Group.description: The following network parameters are intended for use if the system is to act as a host only. A system is considered host only if the system has a single interface, or has multiple interfaces but will not be configured as a router.

Rule.title: 3.1.1 Ensure IP forwarding is disabled
Rule.description: The net.ipv4.ip_forward flag is used to tell the system whether it can forward packets or not.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Setting the flag to 0 ensures that a system with multiple interfaces (for example, a hard proxy), will never be able to forward packets, and therefore, never serve as a router.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameter in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.1.2 Ensure packet redirect sending is disabled
Rule.description: ICMP Redirects are used to send routing information to other hosts. As a host itself does not act as a router (in a host only configuration), there is no need to send redirects.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">An attacker could use a compromised host to send invalid ICMP redirects to other router devices in an attempt to corrupt routing and have users access a system set up by the attacker as opposed to a valid system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects = 0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects = 0 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects <xhtml:span>=0</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 3.2. Network Parameters (Host and Router)
Group.description: The following network parameters are intended for use on both host only and router systems. A system acts as a router if it has at least two interfaces and is configured to perform routing functions.

Rule.title: 3.2.1 Ensure source routed packets are not accepted
Rule.description: In networking, source routing allows a sender to partially or fully specify the route packets take through a network. In contrast, non-source routed packets travel a path determined by routers in the network. In some cases, systems may not be routable or reachable from some locations (e.g. private addresses vs. Internet routable), and so source routed packets would need to be used.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Setting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route </xhtml:span> to 0 disables the system from accepting source routed packets. Assume this system was capable of routing packets to Internet routable addresses on one interface and private addresses on another interface. Assume that the private addresses were not routable to the Internet routable addresses and vice versa. Under normal routing circumstances, an attacker from the Internet routable addresses could not use the system as a way to reach the private address systems. If, however, source routed packets were allowed, they could be used to gain access to the private address systems as the route could be specified, rather than rely on routing protocols that did not allow this routing. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv4. <xhtml:span>conf.default.accept_source_route = 0</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.2 Ensure ICMP redirects are not accepted
Rule.description: ICMP redirect messages are packets that convey routing information and tell your host (acting as a router) to send packets via an alternate path. It is a way of allowing an outside routing device to update your system routing tables. By setting net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects to 0, the system will not accept any ICMP redirect messages, and therefore, won't allow outsiders to update the system's routing tables.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Attackers could use bogus ICMP redirect messages to maliciously alter the system routing tables and get them to send packets to incorrect networks and allow your system packets to be captured.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.3 Ensure secure ICMP redirects are not accepted
Rule.description: Secure ICMP redirects are the same as ICMP redirects, except they come from gateways listed on the default gateway list. It is assumed that these gateways are known to your system, and that they are likely to be secure.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is still possible for even known gateways to be compromised. Setting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv4.conf.all.secure_redirects </xhtml:span> to 0 protects the system from routing table updates by possibly compromised known gateways. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv4.conf.all.secure_redirects = 0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv4.conf.default.secure_redirects = 0 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.secure_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.default.secure_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.4 Ensure suspicious packets are logged
Rule.description: When enabled, this feature logs packets with un-routable source addresses to the kernel log.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Enabling this feature and logging these packets allows an administrator to investigate the possibility that an attacker is sending spoofed packets to their system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians = 1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv4.conf.default.log_martians = 1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.default.log_martians=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.5 Ensure broadcast ICMP requests are ignored
Rule.description: Setting net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts to 1 will cause the system to ignore all ICMP echo and timestamp requests to broadcast and multicast addresses.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Accepting ICMP echo and timestamp requests with broadcast or multicast destinations for your network could be used to trick your host into starting (or participating) in a Smurf attack. A Smurf attack relies on an attacker sending large amounts of ICMP broadcast messages with a spoofed source address. All hosts receiving this message and responding would send echo-reply messages back to the spoofed address, which is probably not routable. If many hosts respond to the packets, the amount of traffic on the network could be significantly multiplied.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameter in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts = 1</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.6 Ensure bogus ICMP responses are ignored
Rule.description: Setting icmp_ignore_bogus_error_responses to 1 prevents the kernel from logging bogus responses (RFC-1122 non-compliant) from broadcast reframes, keeping file systems from filling up with useless log messages.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Some routers (and some attackers) will send responses that violate RFC-1122 and attempt to fill up a log file system with many useless error messages.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameter in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">net.ipv4.icmp_ignore_bogus_error_responses = 1</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.icmp_ignore_bogus_error_responses=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.7 Ensure Reverse Path Filtering is enabled
Rule.description: Setting net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter and net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter to 1 forces the Linux kernel to utilize reverse path filtering on a received packet to determine if the packet was valid. Essentially, with reverse path filtering, if the return packet does not go out the same interface that the corresponding source packet came from, the packet is dropped (and logged if log_martians is set).
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Setting these flags is a good way to deter attackers from sending your system bogus packets that cannot be responded to. One instance where this feature breaks down is if asymmetrical routing is employed. This would occur when using dynamic routing protocols (bgp, ospf, etc) on your system. If you are using asymmetrical routing on your system, you will not be able to enable this feature without breaking the routing.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter = 1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.2.8 Ensure TCP SYN Cookies is enabled
Rule.description: When tcp_syncookies is set, the kernel will handle TCP SYN packets normally until the half-open connection queue is full, at which time, the SYN cookie functionality kicks in. SYN cookies work by not using the SYN queue at all. Instead, the kernel simply replies to the SYN with a SYN|ACK, but will include a specially crafted TCP sequence number that encodes the source and destination IP address and port number and the time the packet was sent. A legitimate connection would send the ACK packet of the three way handshake with the specially crafted sequence number. This allows the system to verify that it has received a valid response to a SYN cookie and allow the connection, even though there is no corresponding SYN in the queue.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Attackers use SYN flood attacks to perform a denial of service attacked on a system by sending many SYN packets without completing the three way handshake. This will quickly use up slots in the kernel's half-open connection queue and prevent legitimate connections from succeeding. SYN cookies allow the system to keep accepting valid connections, even if under a denial of service attack.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameter in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 3.3. IPv6
Group.description: IPv6 is a networking protocol that supersedes IPv4. It has more routable addresses and has built in security. If IPv6 is to be used, follow this section of the benchmark to configure IPv6, otherwise disable IPv6.

Rule.title: 3.3.1 Ensure IPv6 router advertisements are not accepted
Rule.description: This setting disables the system's ability to accept IPv6 router advertisements.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">It is recommended that systems not accept router advertisements as they could be tricked into routing traffic to compromised machines. Setting hard routes within the system (usually a single default route to a trusted router) protects the system from bad routes.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra = 0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra = 0 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv6.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.3.2 Ensure IPv6 redirects are not accepted
Rule.description: This setting prevents the system from accepting ICMP redirects. ICMP redirects tell the system about alternate routes for sending traffic.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">It is recommended that systems not accept ICMP redirects as they could be tricked into routing traffic to compromised machines. Setting hard routes within the system (usually a single default route to a trusted router) protects the system from bad routes.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_redirects=0 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # sysctl -w net.ipv6.route.flush=1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.3.3 Ensure IPv6 is disabled
Rule.description: Although IPv6 has many advantages over IPv4, few organizations have implemented IPv6.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If IPv6 is not to be used, it is recommended that it be disabled to reduce the attack surface of the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/default/grub</xhtml:span> and add <xhtml:span class="inline_block">'</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">ipv6.disable=1'</xhtml:span> to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="ipv6.disable=1"</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to update the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grub2</xhtml:span> configuration: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># update-grub</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.4.1 Ensure TCP Wrappers is installed
Rule.description: TCP Wrappers provides a simple access list and standardized logging method for services capable of supporting it. In the past, services that were called from inetd and xinetd supported the use of tcp wrappers. As inetd and xinetd have been falling in disuse, any service that can support tcp wrappers will have the libwrap.so library attached to it.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">TCP Wrappers provide a good simple access list mechanism to services that may not have that support built in. It is recommended that all services that can support TCP Wrappers, use it.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to install TCP Wrappers:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">apt-get install tcpd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.4.2 Ensure /etc/hosts.allow is configured
Rule.description: The /etc/hosts.allow file specifies which IP addresses are permitted to connect to the host. It is intended to be used in conjunction with the /etc/hosts.deny file.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.allow </xhtml:span> file supports access control by IP and helps ensure that only authorized systems can connect to the system. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to create <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.allow</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # echo "ALL: <xhtml:em><net></xhtml:em> / <xhtml:em><mask></xhtml:em> , <xhtml:em><net></xhtml:em> / <xhtml:em><mask></xhtml:em> , ..." >/etc/hosts.allow </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> where each <xhtml:em><net>/<mask></xhtml:em> combination (for example, "192.168.1.0/255.255.255.0") represents one network block in use by your organization that requires access to this system. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.4.3 Ensure /etc/hosts.deny is configured
Rule.description: The /etc/hosts.deny file specifies which IP addresses are not permitted to connect to the host. It is intended to be used in conjunction with the /etc/hosts.allow file.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.deny </xhtml:span> file serves as a failsafe so that any host not specified in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.allow </xhtml:span> is denied access to the system. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to create <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.deny</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># echo "ALL: ALL" >> /etc/hosts.deny</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.4.4 Ensure permissions on /etc/hosts.allow are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/hosts.allow file contains networking information that is used by many applications and therefore must be readable for these applications to operate.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.allow </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized write access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.allow</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/hosts.allow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 644 /etc/hosts.allow </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.4.5 Ensure permissions on /etc/hosts.deny are 644
Rule.description: The /etc/hosts.deny file contains network information that is used by many system applications and therefore must be readable for these applications to operate.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.deny </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized write access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts.deny</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/hosts.deny <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 644 /etc/hosts.deny </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 3.5. Uncommon Network Protocols
Group.description:
The Linux kernel modules support several network protocols that are not commonly used. If these protocols are not needed, it is recommended that they be disabled in the kernel.
Note: This should not be considered a comprehensive list of uncommon network protocols, you may wish to consider additions to those listed here for your environment.

Rule.title: 3.5.1 Ensure DCCP is disabled
Rule.description: The Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) is a transport layer protocol that supports streaming media and telephony. DCCP provides a way to gain access to congestion control, without having to do it at the application layer, but does not provide in-sequence delivery.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> If the protocol is not required, it is recommended that the drivers not be installed <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> to reduce the potential attack surface. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit or create the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/CIS.conf </xhtml:span> and add the following line: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">install dccp /bin/true</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.5.2 Ensure SCTP is disabled
Rule.description: The Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) is a transport layer protocol used to support message oriented communication, with several streams of messages in one connection. It serves a similar function as TCP and UDP, incorporating features of both. It is message-oriented like UDP, and ensures reliable in-sequence transport of messages with congestion control like TCP.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the protocol is not being used, it is recommended that kernel module not be loaded, disabling the service to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit or create the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/CIS.conf </xhtml:span> and add the following line: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">install sctp /bin/true</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.5.3 Ensure RDS is disabled
Rule.description: The Reliable Datagram Sockets (RDS) protocol is a transport layer protocol designed to provide low-latency, high-bandwidth communications between cluster nodes. It was developed by the Oracle Corporation.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the protocol is not being used, it is recommended that kernel module not be loaded, disabling the service to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit or create the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/CIS.conf </xhtml:span> and add the following line: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">install rds /bin/true</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.5.4 Ensure TIPC is disabled
Rule.description: The Transparent Inter-Process Communication (TIPC) protocol is designed to provide communication between cluster nodes.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the protocol is not being used, it is recommended that kernel module not be loaded, disabling the service to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit or create the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/CIS.conf </xhtml:span> and add the following line: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">install tipc /bin/true</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 3.6. Firewall Configuration
Group.description:
IPtables is an application that allows a system administrator to configure the IPv4 tables, chains and rules provided by the Linux kernel firewall. While several methods of configuration exist this section is intended only to ensure the resulting IPtables rules are in place, not how they are configured. If IPv6 is in use in your environment, similar settings should be applied to the IP6tables as well.
Note: This section broadly assumes starting with an empty IPtables firewall ruleset (established by flushing the rules with iptables -F). Remediation steps included only affect the live system, you will also need to configure your default firewall configuration to apply on boot. Configuration of a live systems firewall directly over a remote connection will often result in being locked out. It is advised to have a known good firewall configuration set to run on boot and to configure an entire firewall structure in a script that is then run and tested before saving to boot. The following script will implement the firewall rules of this section and open port 22(ssh) from anywhere: #!/bin/bash # Flush IPtables rulesiptables -F # Ensure default deny firewall policyiptables -P INPUT DROPiptables -P OUTPUT DROPiptables -P FORWARD DROP # Ensure loopback traffic is configurediptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPTiptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPTiptables -A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 -j DROP # Ensure outbound and established connections are configurediptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPTiptables -A OUTPUT -p udp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPTiptables -A OUTPUT -p icmp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPTiptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPTiptables -A INPUT -p udp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPTiptables -A INPUT -p icmp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT # Open inbound ssh(tcp port 22) connectionsiptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m state --state NEW -j ACCEPT
Ubuntu is distributed with the UFW service which acts as a front end to iptables. The default configuration of UFW implements a configuration very similar to that recommended here. IPTables configuration allows for far more complex implementations than those listed here which may satisfy the intent of these recommendations without strictly matching the examples provided. Note: UFW may interfere with sysctl settings.

Rule.title: 3.6.1 Ensure iptables is installed
Rule.description: iptables allows configuration of the IPv4 tables in the linux kernel and the rules stored within them. Most firewall configuration utilities operate as a front end to iptables.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">iptables is required for firewall management and configuration.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to install <xhtml:span class="inline_block">iptables</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">
<xhtml:span># apt-get install iptables</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.6.2 Ensure default deny firewall policy
Rule.description: A default deny all policy on connections ensures that any unconfigured network usage will be rejected.
