Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">With a default accept policy the firewall will accept any packet that is not configured to be denied. It is easier to white list acceptable usage than to black list unacceptable usage.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to implement a default DROP policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # iptables -P INPUT DROP <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -P OUTPUT DROP <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -P FORWARD DROP </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.6.3 Ensure loopback traffic is configured
Rule.description: Configure the loopback interface to accept traffic. Configure all other interfaces to deny traffic to the loopback network (127.0.0.0/8).
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Loopback traffic is generated between processes on machine and is typically critical to operation of the system. The loopback interface is the only place that loopback network (127.0.0.0/8) traffic should be seen, all other interfaces should ignore traffic on this network as an anti-spoofing measure.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to implement the loopback rules:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 -j DROP </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.6.4 Ensure outbound and established connections are configured
Rule.description: Configure the firewall rules for new outbound, and established connections.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If rules are not in place for new outbound, and established connections all packets will be dropped by the default policy preventing network usage.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Configure iptables in accordance with site policy. The following commands will implement a policy to allow all outbound connections and all established connections:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
<xhtml:span> # iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span> # iptables -A OUTPUT -p icmp -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -A INPUT -p udp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # iptables -A INPUT -p icmp -m state --state ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT </xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.6.5 Ensure firewall rules exist for all open ports
Rule.description: Any ports that have been opened on non-loopback addresses need firewall rules to govern traffic.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Without a firewall rule configured for open ports default firewall policy will drop all packets to these ports.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For each port identified in the audit which does not have a firewall rule establish a proper rule for accepting inbound connections:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # iptables -A INPUT -p <xhtml:em><protocol></xhtml:em> --dport <xhtml:em><port></xhtml:em> -m state --state NEW -j ACCEPT </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 3.7 Ensure wireless interfaces are disabled
Rule.description: Wireless networking is used when wired networks are unavailable. Ubuntu contains a wireless tool kit to allow system administrators to configure and use wireless networks.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If wireless is not to be used, wireless devices can be disabled to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to disable any wireless interfaces:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # ip link set <xhtml:em><interface></xhtml:em> down </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Disable any wireless interfaces in your network configuration.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many if not all laptop workstations and some desktop workstations will connect via wireless requiring these interfaces be enabled.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 4. Logging and Auditing
Group.description:
The items in this section describe how to configure logging, log monitoring, and auditing, using tools included in most distributions. It is recommended that rsyslog be used for logging (with logwatch providing summarization) and auditd be used for auditing (with aureport providing summarization) to automatically monitor logs for intrusion attempts and other suspicious system behavior. In addition to the local log files created by the steps in this section, it is also recommended that sites collect copies of their system logs on a secure, centralized log server via an encrypted connection. Not only does centralized logging help sites correlate events that may be occurring on multiple systems, but having a second copy of the system log information may be critical after a system compromise where the attacker has modified the local log files on the affected system(s). If a log correlation system is deployed, configure it to process the logs described in this section. Because it is often necessary to correlate log information from many different systems (particularly after a security incident) it is recommended that the time be synchronized among systems and devices connected to the local network. The standard Internet protocol for time synchronization is the Network Time Protocol (NTP), which is supported by most network-ready devices. See the ntpd(8) manual page for more information on configuring NTP. It is important that all logs described in this section be monitored on a regular basis and correlated to determine trends. A seemingly innocuous entry in one log could be more significant when compared to an entry in another log.
Note on log file permissions: There really isn't a "one size fits all" solution to the permissions on log files. Many sites utilize group permissions so that administrators who are in a defined security group, such as "wheel" do not have to elevate privileges to root in order to read log files. Also, if a third party log aggregation tool is used, it may need to have group permissions to read the log files, which is preferable to having it run setuid to root. Therefore, there are two remediation and audit steps for log file permissions. One is for systems that do not have a secured group method implemented that only permits root to read the log files (root:root 600). The other is for sites that do have such a setup and are designated as root:securegrp 640 where securegrp is the defined security group (in some cases wheel).

Group.title: 4.1. Configure System Accounting (auditd)
Group.description:
System auditing, through auditd, allows system administrators to monitor their systems such that they can detect unauthorized access or modification of data. By default, auditd will audit SELinux AVC denials, system logins, account modifications, and authentication events. Events will be logged to /var/log/audit/audit.log. The recording of these events will use a modest amount of disk space on a system. If significantly more events are captured, additional on system or off system storage may need to be allocated.
The recommendations in this section implement an audit policy that produces large quantities of logged data. In some environments it can be challenging to store or process these logs and as such they are marked as Level 2 for both Servers and Workstations.
Note: For 64 bit systems that have arch as a rule parameter, you will need two rules: one for 64 bit and one for 32 bit systems. For 32 bit systems, only one rule is needed.
Note: Once all configuration changes have been made to /etc/audit/audit.rules, the auditd configuration must be reloaded: # service auditd reload

Group.title: 4.1.1. Configure Data Retention
Group.description: When auditing, it is important to carefully configure the storage requirements for audit logs. By default, auditd will max out the log files at 5MB and retain only 4 copies of them. Older versions will be deleted. It is possible on a system that the 20 MBs of audit logs may fill up the system causing loss of audit data. While the recommendations here provide guidance, check your site policy for audit storage requirements.

Rule.title: 4.1.1.1 Ensure audit log storage size is configured
Rule.description: Configure the maximum size of the audit log file. Once the log reaches the maximum size, it will be rotated and a new log file will be started.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">It is important that an appropriate size is determined for log files so that they do not impact the system and audit data is not lost.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf</xhtml:span> in accordance with site policy: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> max_log_file = <xhtml:em><MB></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.1.2 Ensure system is disabled when audit logs are full
Rule.description: The auditd daemon can be configured to halt the system when the audit logs are full.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">In high security contexts, the risk of detecting unauthorized access or nonrepudiation exceeds the benefit of the system's availability.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameters in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf:</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> space_left_action = email <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> action_mail_acct = root <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> admin_space_left_action = halt </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.1.3 Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted
Rule.description: The max_log_file_action setting determines how to handle the audit log file reaching the max file size. A value of keep_logs will rotate the logs but never delete old logs.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">In high security contexts, the benefits of maintaining a long audit history exceed the cost of storing the audit history.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf:</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">max_log_file_action = keep_logs</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.2 Ensure auditd service is enabled
Rule.description: Turn on the auditd daemon to record system events.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The capturing of system events provides system administrators with information to allow them to determine if unauthorized access to their system is occurring.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to enable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># update-rc.d auditd enable</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.3 Ensure auditing for processes that start prior to auditd is enabled
Rule.description: Configure grub so that processes that are capable of being audited can be audited even if they start up prior to auditd startup.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Audit events need to be captured on processes that start up prior to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> , so that potential malicious activity cannot go undetected. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/default/grub</xhtml:span> and add audit=1 to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1"</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to update the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grub2</xhtml:span> configuration: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># update-grub</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.4 Ensure events that modify date and time information are collected
Rule.description: Capture events where the system date and/or time has been modified. The parameters in this section are set to determine if the adjtimex (tune kernel clock), settimeofday (Set time, using timeval and timezone structures) stime (using seconds since 1/1/1970) or clock_settime (allows for the setting of several internal clocks and timers) system calls have been executed and always write an audit record to the /var/log/audit.log file upon exit, tagging the records with the identifier "time-change"
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Unexpected changes in system date and/or time could be a sign of malicious activity on the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S adjtimex -S settimeofday -S stime -k time-change <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S clock_settime -k time-change <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/localtime -p wa -k time-change </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S adjtimex -S settimeofday -k time-change <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S adjtimex -S settimeofday -S stime -k time-change <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S clock_settime -k time-change <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S clock_settime -k time-change <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/localtime -p wa -k time-change </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.5 Ensure events that modify user/group information are collected
Rule.description: Record events affecting the group, passwd (user IDs), shadow and gshadow (passwords) or /etc/security/opasswd (old passwords, based on remember parameter in the PAM configuration) files. The parameters in this section will watch the files to see if they have been opened for write or have had attribute changes (e.g. permissions) and tag them with the identifier "identity" in the audit log file.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Unexpected changes to these files could be an indication that the system has been compromised and that an unauthorized user is attempting to hide their activities or compromise additional accounts.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /etc/group -p wa -k identity <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k identity <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/gshadow -p wa -k identity <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/shadow -p wa -k identity <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/security/opasswd -p wa -k identity </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.6 Ensure events that modify the system's network environment are collected
Rule.description: Record changes to network environment files or system calls. The below parameters monitor the sethostname (set the systems host name) or setdomainname (set the systems domainname) system calls, and write an audit event on system call exit. The other parameters monitor the /etc/issue and /etc/issue.net files (messages displayed pre-login), /etc/hosts (file containing host names and associated IP addresses) and /etc/sysconfig/network (directory containing network interface scripts and configurations) files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Monitoring <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sethostname </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">setdomainname </xhtml:span> will identify potential unauthorized changes to host and domainname of a system. The changing of these names could potentially break security parameters that are set based on those names. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts </xhtml:span> file is monitored for changes in the file that can indicate an unauthorized intruder is trying to change machine associations with IP addresses and trick users and processes into connecting to unintended machines. Monitoring <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/issue </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/issue.net </xhtml:span> is important, as intruders could put disinformation into those files and trick users into providing information to the intruder. Monitoring <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysconfig/network </xhtml:span> is important as it can show if network interfaces or scripts are being modified in a way that can lead to the machine becoming unavailable or compromised. All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "system-locale." </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit <xhtml:span> -F arch=b32 -S sethostname -S setdomainname -k system-locale</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/issue -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/issue.net -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/hosts -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/network -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/networks -p wa -k system-locale </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit <xhtml:span> -F arch=b64 -S sethostname -S setdomainname -k system-locale</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit <xhtml:span> -F arch=b32 -S sethostname -S setdomainname -k system-locale</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/issue -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/issue.net -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/hosts -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/network -p wa -k system-locale <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/networks -p wa -k system-locale </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.7 Ensure events that modify the system's Mandatory Access Controls are collected
Rule.description: Monitor SELinux/AppArmor mandatory access controls. The parameters below monitor any write access (potential additional, deletion or modification of files in the directory) or attribute changes to the /etc/selinux or /etc/apparmor and /etc/apparmor.d directories.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Changes to files in these directories could indicate that an unauthorized user is attempting to modify access controls and change security contexts, leading to a compromise of the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> On systems using SELinux add the following line to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules</xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">-w /etc/selinux/ -p wa -k MAC-policy</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> On systems using AppArmor add the following line to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules</xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:div>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /etc/apparmor/ -p wa -k MAC-policy <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/apparmor.d/ -p wa -k MAC-policy </xhtml:code>
</xhtml:div>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.8 Ensure login and logout events are collected
Rule.description: Monitor login and logout events. The parameters below track changes to files associated with login/logout events. The file /var/log/faillog tracks failed events from login. The file /var/log/lastlog maintain records of the last time a user successfully logged in. The file /var/log/tallylog maintains records of failures via the pam_tally2 module
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Monitoring login/logout events could provide a system administrator with information associated with brute force attacks against user logins.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /var/log/faillog -p wa -k logins <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /var/log/lastlog -p wa -k logins <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /var/log/tallylog -p wa -k logins </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.9 Ensure session initiation information is collected
Rule.description: Monitor session initiation events. The parameters in this section track changes to the files associated with session events. The file /var/run/utmp file tracks all currently logged in users. The /var/log/wtmp file tracks logins, logouts, shutdown, and reboot events. All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "session." The file /var/log/btmp keeps track of failed login attempts and can be read by entering the command /usr/bin/last -f /var/log/btmp. All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "logins."
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Monitoring these files for changes could alert a system administrator to logins occurring at unusual hours, which could indicate intruder activity (i.e. a user logging in at a time when they do not normally log in).</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /var/run/utmp -p wa -k session <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /var/log/wtmp -p wa -k session <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /var/log/btmp -p wa -k session </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.10 Ensure discretionary access control permission modification events are collected
Rule.description: Monitor changes to file permissions, attributes, ownership and group. The parameters in this section track changes for system calls that affect file permissions and attributes. The chmod, fchmod and fchmodat system calls affect the permissions associated with a file. The chown, fchown, fchownat and lchown system calls affect owner and group attributes on a file. The setxattr, lsetxattr, fsetxattr (set extended file attributes) and removexattr, lremovexattr, fremovexattr (remove extended file attributes) control extended file attributes. In all cases, an audit record will only be written for non-system user ids (auid >= 1000) and will ignore Daemon events (auid = 4294967295). All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "perm_mod."
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Monitoring for changes in file attributes could alert a system administrator to activity that could indicate intruder activity or policy violation.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S chmod -S fchmod -S fchmodat -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S chown -S fchown -S fchownat -S lchown -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S fsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -S fremovexattr -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S chmod -S fchmod -S fchmodat -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S chmod -S fchmod -S fchmodat -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S chown -S fchown -S fchownat -S lchown -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span> -F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S chown -S fchown -S fchownat -S lchown -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S fsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -S fremovexattr -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S fsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -S fremovexattr -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.11 Ensure unsuccessful unauthorized file access attempts are collected
Rule.description: Monitor for unsuccessful attempts to access files. The parameters below are associated with system calls that control creation (creat), opening (open, openat) and truncation (truncate, ftruncate) of files. An audit log record will only be written if the user is a non-privileged user (auid > = 1000), is not a Daemon event (auid=4294967295) and if the system call returned EACCES (permission denied to the file) or EPERM (some other permanent error associated with the specific system call). All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "access."
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Failed attempts to open, create or truncate files could be an indication that an individual or process is trying to gain unauthorized access to the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S creat -S open -S openat -S truncate -S ftruncate -F exit=-EACCES -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k access</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S creat -S open -S openat -S truncate -S ftruncate -F exit=-EPERM -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k access</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S creat -S open -S openat -S truncate -S ftruncate -F exit=-EACCES -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k access</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S creat -S open -S openat -S truncate -S ftruncate -F exit=-EACCES -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k access</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S creat -S open -S openat -S truncate -S ftruncate -F exit=-EPERM -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k access</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S creat -S open -S openat -S truncate -S ftruncate -F exit=-EPERM -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k access</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.12 Ensure use of privileged commands is collected
Rule.description: Monitor privileged programs (those that have the setuid and/or setgid bit set on execution) to determine if unprivileged users are running these commands.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Execution of privileged commands by non-privileged users could be an indication of someone trying to gain unauthorized access to the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>To remediate this issue, the system administrator will have to execute a find command to locate all the privileged programs and then add an audit line for each one of them. The audit parameters associated with this are as follows:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-F path=" $1 "</xhtml:span> - will populate each file name found through the find command and processed by awk. <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-F perm=x</xhtml:span> - will write an audit record if the file is executed. <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-F auid>=1000</xhtml:span> - will write a record if the user executing the command is not a privileged user. <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-F auid!= 4294967295</xhtml:span> - will ignore Daemon events </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>All audit records should be tagged with the identifier "privileged".</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command replacing <xhtml:em><partition></xhtml:em> with a list of partitions where programs can be executed from on your system: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # find <xhtml:em><partition></xhtml:em> -xdev \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -type f | awk '{print \ <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> "-a always,exit -F path=" $1 " -F perm=x -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 \</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -k privileged" }' </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Add all resulting lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.13 Ensure successful file system mounts are collected
Rule.description: Monitor the use of the mount system call. The mount (and umount) system call controls the mounting and unmounting of file systems. The parameters below configure the system to create an audit record when the mount system call is used by a non-privileged user
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is highly unusual for a non privileged user to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount </xhtml:span> file systems to the system. While tracking <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount</xhtml:span> commands gives the system administrator evidence that external media may have been mounted (based on a review of the source of the mount and confirming it's an external media type), it does not conclusively indicate that data was exported to the media. System administrators who wish to determine if data were exported, would also have to track successful <xhtml:span class="inline_block">open</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">creat </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">truncate </xhtml:span> system calls requiring write access to a file under the mount point of the external media file system. This could give a fair indication that a write occurred. The only way to truly prove it, would be to track successful writes to the external media. Tracking write system calls could quickly fill up the audit log and is not recommended. Recommendations on configuration options to track data export to media is beyond the scope of this document. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S mount -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k mounts</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S mount -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k mounts</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S mount -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k mounts</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.14 Ensure file deletion events by users are collected
Rule.description: Monitor the use of system calls associated with the deletion or renaming of files and file attributes. This configuration statement sets up monitoring for the unlink (remove a file), unlinkat (remove a file attribute), rename (rename a file) and renameat (rename a file attribute) system calls and tags them with the identifier "delete".
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Monitoring these calls from non-privileged users could provide a system administrator with evidence that inappropriate removal of files and file attributes associated with protected files is occurring. While this audit option will look at all events, system administrators will want to look for specific privileged files that are being deleted or altered.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S unlink -S unlinkat -S rename -S renameat -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k delete</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S unlink -S unlinkat -S rename -S renameat -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k delete</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S unlink -S unlinkat -S rename -S renameat -F auid>=1000 <xhtml:span>-F auid!=4294967295 -k delete</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.15 Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected
Rule.description: Monitor scope changes for system administrations. If the system has been properly configured to force system administrators to log in as themselves first and then use the sudo command to execute privileged commands, it is possible to monitor changes in scope. The file /etc/sudoers will be written to when the file or its attributes have changed. The audit records will be tagged with the identifier "scope."
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Changes in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers </xhtml:span> file can indicate that an unauthorized change has been made to scope of system administrator activity. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following line to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.16 Ensure system administrator actions (sudolog) are collected
Rule.description: Monitor the sudo log file. If the system has been properly configured to disable the use of the su command and force all administrators to have to log in first and then use sudo to execute privileged commands, then all administrator commands will be logged to /var/log/sudo.log. Any time a command is executed, an audit event will be triggered as the /var/log/sudo.log file will be opened for write and the executed administration command will be written to the log.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Changes in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/sudo.log </xhtml:span> indicate that an administrator has executed a command or the log file itself has been tampered with. Administrators will want to correlate the events written to the audit trail with the records written to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/sudo.log </xhtml:span> to verify if unauthorized commands have been executed. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">-w /var/log/sudo.log -p wa -k actions</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.17 Ensure kernel module loading and unloading is collected
Rule.description: Monitor the loading and unloading of kernel modules. The programs insmod (install a kernel module), rmmod (remove a kernel module), and modprobe (a more sophisticated program to load and unload modules, as well as some other features) control loading and unloading of modules. The init_module (load a module) and delete_module (delete a module) system calls control loading and unloading of modules. Any execution of the loading and unloading module programs and system calls will trigger an audit record with an identifier of "modules".
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Monitoring the use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">insmod</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rmmod </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">modprobe </xhtml:span> could provide system administrators with evidence that an unauthorized user loaded or unloaded a kernel module, possibly compromising the security of the system. Monitoring of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">init_module </xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">delete_module </xhtml:span> system calls would reflect an unauthorized user attempting to use a different program to load and unload modules. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 32 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /sbin/insmod -p x -k modules <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /sbin/rmmod -p x -k modules <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /sbin/modprobe -p x -k modules <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit arch=b32 -S init_module -S delete_module -k modules </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For 64 bit systems add the following lines to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> -w /sbin/insmod -p x -k modules <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /sbin/rmmod -p x -k modules <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -w /sbin/modprobe -p x -k modules <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> -a always,exit arch=b64 -S init_module -S delete_module -k modules </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.1.18 Ensure the audit configuration is immutable
Rule.description: Set system audit so that audit rules cannot be modified with auditctl. Setting the flag "-e 2" forces audit to be put in immutable mode. Audit changes can only be made on system reboot.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">In immutable mode, unauthorized users cannot execute changes to the audit system to potentially hide malicious activity and then put the audit rules back. Users would most likely notice a system reboot and that could alert administrators of an attempt to make unauthorized audit changes.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following line to the end of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules </xhtml:span> file. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">-e 2</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 4.2. Configure Logging
Group.description: Logging services should be configured to prevent information leaks and to aggregate logs on a remote server so that they can be reviewed in the event of a system compromise and ease log analysis.

Group.title: 4.2.1. Configure rsyslog
Group.description:
The rsyslog software is recommended as a replacement for the syslogd daemon and provides improvements over syslogd, such as connection-oriented (i.e. TCP) transmission of logs, the option to log to database formats, and the encryption of log data en route to a central logging server.
Note: This section only applies if rsyslog is installed on the system.

Rule.title: 4.2.1.1 Ensure rsyslog Service is enabled
Rule.description: Once the rsyslog package is installed it needs to be activated.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> service is not activated the system may default to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslogd</xhtml:span> service or lack logging instead. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to enable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl enable rsyslog</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.1.2 Ensure logging is configured
Rule.description: The /etc/rsyslog.conf file specifies rules for logging and which files are to be used to log certain classes of messages.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> A great deal of important security-related information is sent via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog </xhtml:span> (e.g., successful and failed su attempts, failed login attempts, root login attempts, etc.). </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the following lines in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/rsyslog.conf </xhtml:span> file as appropriate for your <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> environment: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> *.emerg :omusrmsg:* <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> mail.* -/var/log/mail <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> mail.info -/var/log/mail.info <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> mail.warning -/var/log/mail.warn <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> mail.err /var/log/mail.err <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> news.crit -/var/log/news/news.crit <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> news.err -/var/log/news/news.err <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> news.notice -/var/log/news/news.notice <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> *.=warning;*.=err -/var/log/warn <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> *.crit /var/log/warn <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> *.*;mail.none;news.none -/var/log/messages <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> local0,local1.* -/var/log/localmessages <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> local2,local3.* -/var/log/localmessages <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> local4,local5.* -/var/log/localmessages <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> local6,local7.* -/var/log/localmessages </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to restart <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslogd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pkill -HUP rsyslogd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.1.3 Ensure rsyslog default file permissions configured
Rule.description: rsyslog will create logfiles that do not already exist on the system. This setting controls what permissions will be applied to these newly created files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">It is important to ensure that log files have the correct permissions to ensure that sensitive data is archived and protected.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the /etc/rsyslog.conf and set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">$FileCreateMode</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">$FileCreateMode 0640</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.1.4 Ensure rsyslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host
Rule.description: The rsyslog utility supports the ability to send logs it gathers to a remote log host running syslogd(8) or to receive messages from remote hosts, reducing administrative overhead.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Storing log data on a remote host protects log integrity from local attacks. If an attacker gains root access on the local system, they could tamper with or remove log data that is stored on the local system</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/rsyslog.conf </xhtml:span> file and add the following line (where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">
<xhtml:em>loghost.example.com</xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span> is the name of your central log host). </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">*.* @@loghost.example.com</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to restart <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pkill -HUP rsyslogd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.1.5 Ensure remote rsyslog messages are only accepted on designated log hosts.
Rule.description: By default, rsyslog does not listen for log messages coming in from remote systems. The ModLoad tells rsyslog to load the imtcp.so module so it can listen over a network via TCP. The InputTCPServerRun option instructs rsyslogd to listen on the specified TCP port.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The guidance in the section ensures that remote log hosts are configured to only accept <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog </xhtml:span> data from hosts within the specified domain and that those systems that are not designed to be log hosts do not accept any remote <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog </xhtml:span> messages. This provides protection from spoofed log data and ensures that system administrators are reviewing reasonably complete syslog data in a central location. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> For hosts that are designated as log hosts, edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/rsyslog.conf </xhtml:span> file and un-comment or add the following lines: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> $ModLoad imtcp.so <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> $InputTCPServerRun 514 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> For hosts that are not designated as log hosts, edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/rsyslog.conf </xhtml:span> file and comment or remove the following lines: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # $ModLoad imtcp.so <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # $InputTCPServerRun 514 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to restart <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslogd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pkill -HUP rsyslogd</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 4.2.2. Configure syslog-ng
Group.description:
The syslog-ng software is recommended as a replacement for the syslogd daemon and provides improvements over syslogd, such as connection-oriented (i.e. TCP) transmission of logs, the option to log to database formats, and the encryption of log data en route to a central logging server.
Note: This section only applies if syslog-ng is installed on the system.

Rule.title: 4.2.2.1 Ensure syslog-ng service is enabled
Rule.description: Once the syslog-ng package is installed it needs to be activated.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng</xhtml:span> service is not activated the system may default to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslogd</xhtml:span> service or lack logging instead. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to enable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># update-rc.d syslog-ng enable</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.2.2 Ensure logging is configured
Rule.description: The /etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf file specifies rules for logging and which files are to be used to log certain classes of messages.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> A great deal of important security-related information is sent via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng </xhtml:span> (e.g., successful and failed su attempts, failed login attempts, root login attempts, etc.). </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
                         
    <xhtml:p>
                                
        <xhtml:p>
            Edit the log lines in the 
            <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf </xhtml:span>
            file as appropriate for your
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            environment:
        </xhtml:p>
                                
        <xhtml:code class="code_block">
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_console); destination(console); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_console); destination(xconsole); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_newscrit); destination(newscrit); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_newserr); destination(newserr); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_newsnotice); destination(newsnotice); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_mailinfo); destination(mailinfo); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_mailwarn); destination(mailwarn); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_mailerr); destination(mailerr); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_mail); destination(mail); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_acpid); destination(acpid); flags(final); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_acpid_full); destination(devnull); flags(final); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_acpid_old); destination(acpid); flags(final); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_netmgm); destination(netmgm); flags(final); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_local); destination(localmessages); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_messages); destination(messages); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_iptables); destination(firewall); };
            <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
            log { source(src); source(chroots); filter(f_warn); destination(warn); };
        </xhtml:code>
                                
        <xhtml:p>Run the following command to restart syslog-ng:</xhtml:p>
                                
        <xhtml:code class="code_block"># pkill -HUP syslog-ng</xhtml:code>
                                
        <xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
                             
    </xhtml:p>
                      
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.2.3 Ensure syslog-ng default file permissions configured
Rule.description: syslog-ng will create logfiles that do not already exist on the system. This setting controls what permissions will be applied to these newly created files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is important to ensure that log files exist and have the correct permissions to ensure that sensitive <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng</xhtml:span> data is archived and protected. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf</xhtml:span> and set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">perm</xhtml:span> option to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">options { chain_hostnames(off); flush_lines(0); perm(0640); stats_freq(3600); threaded(yes); };</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.2.4 Ensure syslog-ng is configured to send logs to a remote log host
Rule.description: The syslog-ng utility supports the ability to send logs it gathers to a remote log host or to receive messages from remote hosts, reducing administrative overhead.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Storing log data on a remote host protects log integrity from local attacks. If an attacker gains root access on the local system, they could tamper with or remove log data that is stored on the local system</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block"> / <xhtml:span>etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:span> file and add the following lines (where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">
<xhtml:em>logfile.example.com</xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span> is the name of your central log host). </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> destination logserver { tcp(" <xhtml:em>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">logfile.example.com</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:em> " port(514)); }; log { source(src); destination(logserver); }; </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to restart syslog-ng:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pkill -HUP syslog-ng</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.2.5 Ensure remote syslog-ng messages are only accepted on designated log hosts
Rule.description: By default, syslog-ng does not listen for log messages coming in from remote systems.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The guidance in the section ensures that remote log hosts are configured to only accept <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng </xhtml:span> data from hosts within the specified domain and that those systems that are not designed to be log hosts do not accept any remote <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng </xhtml:span> messages. This provides protection from spoofed log data and ensures that system administrators are reviewing reasonably complete syslog data in a central location. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> On designated log hosts edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf</xhtml:span> file and configure the following lines are appropriately: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> source net{ tcp(); }; <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> destination remote { file("/var/log/remote/${FULLHOST}-log"); }; <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> log { source(net); destination(remote); }; </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> On non designated log hosts edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf</xhtml:span> file and remove or edit any sources that accept network sourced log messages. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to restart <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pkill -HUP syslog-ng</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.3 Ensure rsyslog or syslog-ng is installed
Rule.description: The rsyslog and syslog-ng software are recommended replacements to the original syslogd daemon which provide improvements over syslogd, such as connection-oriented (i.e. TCP) transmission of logs, the option to log to database formats, and the encryption of log data en route to a central logging server.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:span> The security enhancements of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng</xhtml:span> such as connection-oriented (i.e. TCP) transmission of logs, the option to log to database formats, and the encryption of log data en route to a central logging server) justify installing and configuring the package. </xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Install rsyslog or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog-ng</xhtml:span> using one of the following commands: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # apt-get install rsyslog <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # apt-get install syslog-ng </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.2.4 Ensure permissions on all logfiles are configured
Rule.description: Log files stored in /var/log/ contain logged information from many services on the system, or on log hosts others as well.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">It is important to ensure that log files have the correct permissions to ensure that sensitive data is archived and protected.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to set permissions on all existing log files:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chmod -R g-wx,o-rwx /var/log/*</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 4.3 Ensure logrotate is configured
Rule.description: The system includes the capability of rotating log files regularly to avoid filling up the system with logs or making the logs unmanageable large. The file /etc/logrotate.d/syslog is the configuration file used to rotate log files created by syslog or rsyslog.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">By keeping the log files smaller and more manageable, a system administrator can easily archive these files to another system and spend less time looking through inordinately large log files.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/logrotate.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/logrotate.d/</xhtml:span> * to ensure logs are rotated according to site policy. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.1 Ensure cron daemon is enabled
Rule.description: The cron daemon is used to execute batch jobs on the system.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> While there may not be user jobs that need to be run on the system, the system does have maintenance jobs that may include security monitoring that have to run, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron </xhtml:span> is used to execute them. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:span>Run the following command</xhtml:span> to enable <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl enable crond</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.2 Ensure permissions on /etc/crontab are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/crontab file is used by cron to control its own jobs. The commands in this item make sure that root is the user and group owner of the file and that only the owner can access the file.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">This file contains information on what system jobs are run by cron. Write access to these files could provide unprivileged users with the ability to elevate their privileges. Read access to these files could provide users with the ability to gain insight on system jobs that run on the system and could provide them a way to gain unauthorized privileged access.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/crontab</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/crontab <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/crontab </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.3 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.hourly are configured
Rule.description: This directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on an hourly basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Granting write access to this directory for non-privileged users could provide them the means for gaining unauthorized elevated privileges. Granting read access to this directory could give an unprivileged user insight in how to gain elevated privileges or circumvent auditing controls.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.hourly</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/cron.hourly <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.hourly </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.4 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.daily are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/cron.daily directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on a daily basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Granting write access to this directory for non-privileged users could provide them the means for gaining unauthorized elevated privileges. Granting read access to this directory could give an unprivileged user insight in how to gain elevated privileges or circumvent auditing controls.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.daily</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/cron.daily <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.daily </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.5 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.weekly are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/cron.weekly directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on a weekly basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Granting write access to this directory for non-privileged users could provide them the means for gaining unauthorized elevated privileges. Granting read access to this directory could give an unprivileged user insight in how to gain elevated privileges or circumvent auditing controls.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.weekly</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/cron.weekly <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.weekly </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.6 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.monthly are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/cron.monthly directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on a monthly basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Granting write access to this directory for non-privileged users could provide them the means for gaining unauthorized elevated privileges. Granting read access to this directory could give an unprivileged user insight in how to gain elevated privileges or circumvent auditing controls.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.monthly</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
