<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/cron.monthly <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.monthly </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.7 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.d are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/cron.d directory contains system cron jobs that need to run in a similar manner to the hourly, daily weekly and monthly jobs from /etc/crontab, but require more granular control as to when they run. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Granting write access to this directory for non-privileged users could provide them the means for gaining unauthorized elevated privileges. Granting read access to this directory could give an unprivileged user insight in how to gain elevated privileges or circumvent auditing controls.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.d</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/cron.d <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.d </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.1.8 Ensure at/cron is restricted to authorized users
Rule.description: Configure /etc/cron.allow and /etc/at.allow to allow specific users to use these services. If /etc/cron.allow or /etc/at.allow do not exist, then /etc/at.deny and /etc/cron.deny are checked. Any user not specifically defined in those files is allowed to use at and cron. By removing the files, only users in /etc/cron.allow and /etc/at.allow are allowed to use at and cron. Note that even though a given user is not listed in cron.allow, cron jobs can still be run as that user. The cron.allow file only controls administrative access to the crontab command for scheduling and modifying cron jobs.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> On many systems, only the system administrator is authorized to schedule <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron </xhtml:span> jobs. Using the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron.allow </xhtml:span> file to control who can run <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron </xhtml:span> jobs enforces this policy. It is easier to manage an allow list than a deny list. In a deny list, you could potentially add a user ID to the system and forget to add it to the deny files. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to remove <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.deny</xhtml:span> and create and set permissions and ownership for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.allow</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # rm /etc/cron.deny <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # rm /etc/at.deny <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # touch /etc/cron.allow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # touch /etc/at.allow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.allow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod og-rwx /etc/at.allow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chown root:root /etc/cron.allow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chown root:root /etc/at.allow </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 5.2. SSH Server Configuration
Group.description:
SSH is a secure, encrypted replacement for common login services such as telnet, ftp, rlogin, rsh, and rcp. It is strongly recommended that sites abandon older clear-text login protocols and use SSH to prevent session hijacking and sniffing of sensitive data off the network.
Note: The recommendations in this section only apply if the SSH daemon is installed on the system, if remote access is not required the SSH daemon can be removed and this section skipped.
Note: Once all configuration changes have been made to /etc/ssh/sshd_config, the sshd configuration must be reloaded: # service sshd reload

Rule.title: 5.2.1 Ensure permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/ssh/sshd_config file contains configuration specifications for sshd. The command below sets the owner and group of the file to root.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file needs to be protected from unauthorized changes by non-privileged users. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
<xhtml:span># chmod og-rwx /etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.2 Ensure SSH Protocol is set to 2
Rule.description: SSH supports two different and incompatible protocols: SSH1 and SSH2. SSH1 was the original protocol and was subject to security issues. SSH2 is more advanced and secure.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">SSH v1 suffers from insecurities that do not affect SSH v2.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Protocol 2</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.3 Ensure SSH LogLevel is set to INFO
Rule.description: The INFO parameter specifies that login and logout activity will be logged.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> SSH provides several logging levels with varying amounts of verbosity. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DEBUG </xhtml:span> is specifically <xhtml:em>not</xhtml:em> recommended other than strictly for debugging SSH communications since it provides so much data that it is difficult to identify important security information. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">INFO </xhtml:span> level is the basic level that only records login activity of SSH users. In many situations, such as Incident Response, it is important to determine when a particular user was active on a system. The logout record can eliminate those users who disconnected, which helps narrow the field. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">LogLevel INFO</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.4 Ensure SSH X11 forwarding is disabled
Rule.description: The X11Forwarding parameter provides the ability to tunnel X11 traffic through the connection to enable remote graphic connections.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Disable X11 forwarding unless there is an operational requirement to use X11 applications directly. There is a small risk that the remote X11 servers of users who are logged in via SSH with X11 forwarding could be compromised by other users on the X11 server. Note that even if X11 forwarding is disabled, users can always install their own forwarders.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">X11Forwarding no</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.5 Ensure SSH MaxAuthTries is set to 4 or less
Rule.description: The MaxAuthTries parameter specifies the maximum number of authentication attempts permitted per connection. When the login failure count reaches half the number, error messages will be written to the syslog file detailing the login failure.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Setting the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">MaxAuthTries </xhtml:span> parameter to a low number will minimize the risk of successful brute force attacks to the SSH server. While the recommended setting is 4, set the number based on site policy. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">MaxAuthTries 4</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.6 Ensure SSH IgnoreRhosts is enabled
Rule.description: The IgnoreRhosts parameter specifies that .rhosts and .shosts files will not be used in RhostsRSAAuthentication or HostbasedAuthentication.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Setting this parameter forces users to enter a password when authenticating with ssh.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">IgnoreRhosts yes</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.7 Ensure SSH HostbasedAuthentication is disabled
Rule.description: The HostbasedAuthentication parameter specifies if authentication is allowed through trusted hosts via the user of .rhosts, or /etc/hosts.equiv, along with successful public key client host authentication. This option only applies to SSH Protocol Version 2.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Even though the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rhosts </xhtml:span> files are ineffective if support is disabled in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.conf</xhtml:span> , disabling the ability to use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rhosts </xhtml:span> files in SSH provides an additional layer of protection . </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">HostbasedAuthentication no</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.8 Ensure SSH root login is disabled
Rule.description: The PermitRootLogin parameter specifies if the root user can log in using ssh(1). The default is no.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Disallowing root logins over SSH requires system admins to authenticate using their own individual account, then escalating to root via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo </xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> . This in turn limits opportunity for non-repudiation and provides a clear audit trail in the event of a security incident </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PermitRootLogin no</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.9 Ensure SSH PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled
Rule.description: The PermitEmptyPasswords parameter specifies if the SSH server allows login to accounts with empty password strings.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Disallowing remote shell access to accounts that have an empty password reduces the probability of unauthorized access to the system</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PermitEmptyPasswords no</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.10 Ensure SSH PermitUserEnvironment is disabled
Rule.description: The PermitUserEnvironment option allows users to present environment options to the ssh daemon.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Permitting users the ability to set environment variables through the SSH daemon could potentially allow users to bypass security controls (e.g. setting an execution path that has <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh </xhtml:span> executing trojan'd programs) </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PermitUserEnvironment no</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.11 Ensure only approved MAC algorithms are used
Rule.description: This variable limits the types of MAC algorithms that SSH can use during communication.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">MD5 and 96-bit MAC algorithms are considered weak and have been shown to increase exploitability in SSH downgrade attacks. Weak algorithms continue to have a great deal of attention as a weak spot that can be exploited with expanded computing power. An attacker that breaks the algorithm could take advantage of a MiTM position to decrypt the SSH tunnel and capture credentials and information</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">MACs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256,umac-128@openssh.com</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.12 Ensure SSH Idle Timeout Interval is configured
Rule.description: The two options ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax control the timeout of ssh sessions. When the ClientAliveInterval variable is set, ssh sessions that have no activity for the specified length of time are terminated. When the ClientAliveCountMax variable is set, sshd will send client alive messages at every ClientAliveInterval interval. When the number of consecutive client alive messages are sent with no response from the client, the ssh session is terminated. For example, if the ClientAliveInterval is set to 15 seconds and the ClientAliveCountMax is set to 3, the client ssh session will be terminated after 45 seconds of idle time.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Having no timeout value associated with a connection could allow an unauthorized user access to another user's <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh </xhtml:span> session (e.g. user walks away from their computer and doesn't lock the screen). Setting a timeout value at least reduces the risk of this happening.. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> While the recommended setting is 300 seconds (5 minutes), set this timeout value based on site policy. The recommended setting for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax </xhtml:span> is 0. In this case, the client session will be terminated after 5 minutes of idle time and no keepalive messages will be sent. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameters as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> ClientAliveInterval 300 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> ClientAliveCountMax 0 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.13 Ensure SSH LoginGraceTime is set to one minute or less
Rule.description: The LoginGraceTime parameter specifies the time allowed for successful authentication to the SSH server. The longer the Grace period is the more open unauthenticated connections can exist. Like other session controls in this session the Grace Period should be limited to appropriate organizational limits to ensure the service is available for needed access.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Setting the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">LoginGraceTime </xhtml:span> parameter to a low number will minimize the risk of successful brute force attacks to the SSH server. It will also limit the number of concurrent unauthenticated connections While the recommended setting is 60 seconds (1 Minute), set the number based on site policy. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">LoginGraceTime 60</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.14 Ensure SSH access is limited
Rule.description:
There are several options available to limit which users and group can access the system via SSH. It is recommended that at least one of the following options be leveraged:
AllowUsers
The AllowUsers variable gives the system administrator the option of allowing specific users to ssh into the system. The list consists of comma separated user names. Numeric user IDs are not recognized with this variable. If a system administrator wants to restrict user access further by only allowing the allowed users to log in from a particular host, the entry can be specified in the form of user@host.
AllowGroups
The AllowGroups variable gives the system administrator the option of allowing specific groups of users to ssh into the system. The list consists of comma separated group names. Numeric group IDs are not recognized with this variable.
DenyUsers
The DenyUsers variable gives the system administrator the option of denying specific users to ssh into the system. The list consists of comma separated user names. Numeric user IDs are not recognized with this variable. If a system administrator wants to restrict user access further by specifically denying a user's access from a particular host, the entry can be specified in the form of user@host.
DenyGroups
The DenyGroups variable gives the system administrator the option of denying specific groups of users to ssh into the system. The list consists of comma separated group names. Numeric group IDs are not recognized with this variable.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Restricting which users can remotely access the system via SSH will help ensure that only authorized users access the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set one or more of the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> AllowUsers <xhtml:em><userlist></xhtml:em>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> AllowGroups <xhtml:em><grouplist></xhtml:em>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> DenyUsers <xhtml:em><userlist></xhtml:em>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> DenyGroups <xhtml:em><grouplist></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.2.15 Ensure SSH warning banner is configured
Rule.description: The Banner parameter specifies a file whose contents must be sent to the remote user before authentication is permitted. By default, no banner is displayed.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Banners are used to warn connecting users of the particular site's policy regarding connection. <xhtml:span>Presenting a warning message prior to the normal user login may assist the prosecution of trespassers on the computer system.</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config </xhtml:span> file to set the parameter as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Banner /etc/issue.net</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 5.3. Configure PAM
Group.description: PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) is a service that implements modular authentication modules on UNIX systems. PAM is implemented as a set of shared objects that are loaded and executed when a program needs to authenticate a user. Files for PAM are typically located in the /etc/pam.d directory. PAM must be carefully configured to secure system authentication. While this section covers some of PAM, please consult other PAM resources to fully understand the configuration capabilities.

Rule.title: 5.3.1 Ensure password creation requirements are configured
Rule.description:
The pam_pwquality.so module checks the strength of passwords. It performs checks such as making sure a password is not a dictionary word, it is a certain length, contains a mix of characters (e.g. alphabet, numeric, other) and more. The following are definitions of the pam_pwquality.so options.
try_first_pass - retrieve the password from a previous stacked PAM module. If not available, then prompt the user for a password.
retry=3 - Allow 3 tries before sending back a failure.
The following options are set in the /etc/security/pwquality.conf file:
minlen=14 - password must be 14 characters or more
dcredit=-1 - provide at least one digit
ucredit=-1 - provide at least one uppercase character
ocredit=-1 - provide at least one special character
lcredit=-1 - provide at least one lowercase character
The settings shown above are one possible policy. Alter these values to conform to your own organization's password policies.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Strong passwords protect systems from being hacked through brute force methods.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to install the pam_pwquality module:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">apt-get install libpam-pwquality</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-passwd</xhtml:span> file to include the appropriate options for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> and to conform to site policy: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">password requisite pam_pwquality.so try_first_pass retry=3</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> to add or update the following settings to conform to site policy: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> minlen=14 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> dcredit=-1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> ucredit=-1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> ocredit=-1 <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> lcredit=-1 </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.3.2 Ensure lockout for failed password attempts is configured
Rule.description: Lock out users after n unsuccessful consecutive login attempts. The first sets of changes are made to the PAM configuration files. The second set of changes are applied to the program specific PAM configuration file. The second set of changes must be applied to each program that will lock out users. Check the documentation for each secondary program for instructions on how to configure them to work with PAM. Set the lockout number to the policy in effect at your site.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Locking out user IDs after <xhtml:em>n</xhtml:em> unsuccessful consecutive login attempts mitigates brute force password attacks against your systems. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-auth </xhtml:span> file and add the auth line below: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">auth required pam_tally2.so onerr=fail audit silent deny=5 unlock_time=900</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If a user has been locked out because they have reached the maximum consecutive failure count defined by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_tally2.so </xhtml:span> module, the user can be unlocked by issuing the command <xhtml:span class="inline_block"> /sbin/pam_tally2 -u <xhtml:em><username></xhtml:em> --reset </xhtml:span> . This command sets the failed count to 0, effectively unlocking the user. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.3.3 Ensure password reuse is limited
Rule.description: The /etc/security/opasswd file stores the users' old passwords and can be checked to ensure that users are not recycling recent passwords.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Forcing users not to reuse their past 5 passwords make it less likely that an attacker will be able to guess the password.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Note that these change only apply to accounts configured on the local system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> file to include the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">remember</xhtml:span> option and conform to site policy as shown: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">password sufficient pam_unix.so remember=5</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.3.4 Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512
Rule.description: The commands below change password encryption from md5 to sha512 (a much stronger hashing algorithm). All existing accounts will need to perform a password change to upgrade the stored hashes to the new algorithm.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The SHA-512 algorithm provides much stronger hashing than MD5, thus providing additional protection to the system by increasing the level of effort for an attacker to successfully determine passwords.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Note that these change only apply to accounts configured on the local system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> file to include the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> option for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix.so</xhtml:span> as shown: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">password [success=1 default=ignore] pam_unix.so sha512</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 5.4. User Accounts and Environment
Group.description: This section provides guidance on setting up secure defaults for system and user accounts and their environment.

Group.title: 5.4.1. Set Shadow Password Suite Parameters
Group.description: While a majority of the password control parameters have been moved to PAM, some parameters are still available through the shadow password suite. Any changes made to /etc/login.defs will only be applied if the usermod command is used. If user IDs are added a different way, use the chage command to effect changes to individual user IDs.

Rule.title: 5.4.1.1 Ensure password expiration is 90 days or less
Rule.description: The PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to force passwords to expire once they reach a defined age. It is recommended that the PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter be set to less than or equal to 90 days.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">The window of opportunity for an attacker to leverage compromised credentials or successfully compromise credentials via an online brute force attack is limited by the age of the password. Therefore, reducing the maximum age of a password also reduces an attacker's window of opportunity.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> parameter to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">90</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS 90</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chage --maxdays 90 <xhtml:em><user></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.4.1.2 Ensure minimum days between password changes is 7 or more
Rule.description: The PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to prevent users from changing their password until a minimum number of days have passed since the last time the user changed their password. It is recommended that PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter be set to 7 or more days.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">By restricting the frequency of password changes, an administrator can prevent users from repeatedly changing their password in an attempt to circumvent password reuse controls.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span> parameter to <xhtml:span>7</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS 7</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">
<xhtml:span> # chage --mindays 7 <xhtml:em><user></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.4.1.3 Ensure password expiration warning days is 7 or more
Rule.description: The PASS_WARN_AGE parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to notify users that their password will expire in a defined number of days. It is recommended that the PASS_WARN_AGE parameter be set to 7 or more days.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Providing an advance warning that a password will be expiring gives users time to think of a secure password. Users caught unaware may choose a simple password or write it down where it may be discovered.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> parameter to <xhtml:span>7</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_WARN_AGE 7</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">
<xhtml:span> # chage --warndays 7 <xhtml:em><user></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.4.1.4 Ensure inactive password lock is 30 days or less
Rule.description: User accounts that have been inactive for over a given period of time can be automatically disabled. It is recommended that accounts that are inactive for 30 days after password expiration be disabled.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Inactive accounts pose a threat to system security since the users are not logging in to notice failed login attempts or other anomalies.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to set the default password inactivity period to 30 days:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># useradd -D -f 30</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:div>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chage --inactive 30 <xhtml:em><user></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:div>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.4.2 Ensure system accounts are non-login
Rule.description: There are a number of accounts provided with Ubuntu that are used to manage applications and are not intended to provide an interactive shell.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is important to make sure that accounts that are not being used by regular users are prevented from being used to provide an interactive shell. By default, Ubuntu sets the password field for these accounts to an invalid string, but it is also recommended that the shell field in the password file be set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/sbin/nologin</xhtml:span> . This prevents the account from potentially being used to run any commands. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Set the shell for any accounts returned by the audit script to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/sbin/nologin</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin <xhtml:em><user></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> The following script will automatically set all user shells required to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/sbin/nologin</xhtml:span> and lock the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sync</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shutdown</xhtml:span> , and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span> users: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> #!/bin/bash <xhtml:br></xhtml:br>
<xhtml:br></xhtml:br> for user in `awk -F: '($3 < 1000) {print $1 }' /etc/passwd`; do <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> if [ $user != "root" ]; then <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> usermod -L $user <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> if [ $user != "sync" ] && [ $user != "shutdown" ] && [ $user != "halt" ]; then <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin $user <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> fi <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> fi <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> done </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.4.3 Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0
Rule.description: The usermod command can be used to specify which group the root user belongs to. This affects permissions of files that are created by the root user.
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Using GID 0 for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">
<xhtml:em>root</xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span> account helps prevent <xhtml:span class="inline_block">
<xhtml:em>root</xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span> -owned files from accidentally becoming accessible to non-privileged users. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user default group to GID <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># usermod -g 0 root</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.4.4 Ensure default user umask is 027 or more restrictive
Rule.description: The default umask determines the permissions of files created by users. The user creating the file has the discretion of making their files and directories readable by others via the chmod command. Users who wish to allow their files and directories to be readable by others by default may choose a different default umask by inserting the umask command into the standard shell configuration files (.profile, .bashrc, etc.) in their home directories.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Setting a very secure default value for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask </xhtml:span> ensures that users make a conscious choice about their file permissions. A default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask </xhtml:span> setting of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">077 </xhtml:span> causes files and directories created by users to not be readable by any other user on the system. A <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask </xhtml:span> of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">027 </xhtml:span> would make files and directories readable by users in the same Unix group, while a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask </xhtml:span> of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">022 </xhtml:span> would make files readable by every user on the system. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bash.bashrc</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile </xhtml:span> files (and the appropriate files for any other shell supported on your system) and add or edit any umask parameters as follows: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">umask 027</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.5 Ensure root login is restricted to system console
Rule.description: The file /etc/securetty contains a list of valid terminals that may be logged in directly as root.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Since the system console has special properties to handle emergency situations, it is important to ensure that the console is in a physically secure location and that unauthorized consoles have not been defined.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Remove entries for any consoles that are not in a physically secure location.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 5.6 Ensure access to the su command is restricted
Rule.description: The su command allows a user to run a command or shell as another user. The program has been superseded by sudo, which allows for more granular control over privileged access. Normally, the su command can be executed by any user. By uncommenting the pam_wheel.so statement in /etc/pam.d/su, the su command will only allow users in the wheel group to execute su.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Restricting the use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> , and using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo </xhtml:span> in its place, provides system administrators better control of the escalation of user privileges to execute privileged commands. The sudo utility also provides a better logging and audit mechanism, as it can log each command executed via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> , whereas <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su </xhtml:span> can only record that a user executed the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su </xhtml:span> program. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Add the following line to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/su </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> Create a comma separated list of users in the wheel statement in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group </xhtml:span> file: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> wheel:x:10:root, <xhtml:em><user list></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 6. System Maintenance
Group.description: Recommendations in this section are intended as maintenance and are intended to be checked on a frequent basis to ensure system stability. Many recommendations do not have quick remediations and require investigation into the cause and best fix available and may indicate an attempted breach of system security.

Group.title: 6.1. System File Permissions
Group.description: This section provides guidance on securing aspects of system files and directories.

Rule.title: 6.1.1 Audit system file permissions
Rule.description:
The Debian package manager has a number of useful options. One of these, the --verify option, can be used to verify that system packages are correctly installed. The --verify option can be used to verify a particular package or to verify all system packages. If no output is returned, the package is installed correctly. The following table describes the meaning of output from the verify option: Code MeaningS File size differs.M File mode differs (includes permissions and file type).5 The MD5 checksum differs.D The major and minor version numbers differ on a device file.L A mismatch occurs in a link.U The file ownership differs.G The file group owner differs.T The file time (mtime) differs. The dpkg -S command can be used to determine which package a particular file belongs to. For example the following commands determines which package the /bin/bash file belongs to:
# dpkg -S /bin/bashbash: /bin/bash
To verify the settings for the package that controls the /bin/bash file, run the following: # dpkg --verify bash??5?????? c /etc/bash.bashrc
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">It is important to confirm that packaged system files and directories are maintained with the permissions they were intended to have from the OS vendor. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Correct any discrepancies found and rerun the audit until output is clean or risk is mitigated or accepted.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.2 Ensure permissions on /etc/passwd are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/passwd file contains user account information that is used by many system utilities and therefore must be readable for these utilities to operate.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized write access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/passwd <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 644 /etc/passwd </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.3 Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/shadow file is used to store the information about user accounts that is critical to the security of those accounts, such as the hashed password and other security information.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> If attackers can gain read access to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow </xhtml:span> file, they can easily run a password cracking program against the hashed password to break it. Other security information that is stored in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow </xhtml:span> file (such as expiration) could also be useful to subvert the user accounts. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the one following commands to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:shadow /etc/shadow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod o-rwx,g-wx /etc/shadow </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.4 Ensure permissions on /etc/group are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/group file contains a list of all the valid groups defined in the system. The command below allows read/write access for root and read access for everyone else.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group </xhtml:span> file needs to be protected from unauthorized changes by non-privileged users, but needs to be readable as this information is used with many non-privileged programs. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/group <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 644 /etc/group </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.5 Ensure permissions on /etc/gshadow are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/gshadow file is used to store the information about groups that is critical to the security of those accounts, such as the hashed password and other security information.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> If attackers can gain read access to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow </xhtml:span> file, they can easily run a password cracking program against the hashed password to break it. Other security information that is stored in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow </xhtml:span> file (such as group administrators) could also be useful to subvert the group. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the the following commands to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:shadow /etc/gshadow <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod o-rwx,g-rw /etc/gshadow </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.6 Ensure permissions on /etc/passwd- are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/passwd- file contains backup user account information.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd- </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd-</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/passwd- <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 600 /etc/passwd- </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.7 Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow- are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/shadow- file is used to store backup information about user accounts that is critical to the security of those accounts, such as the hashed password and other security information.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow- </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow-</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/shadow- <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 600 /etc/shadow- </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.8 Ensure permissions on /etc/group- are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/group- file contains a backup list of all the valid groups defined in the system.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group- </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group-</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/group- <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 600 /etc/group- </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.9 Ensure permissions on /etc/gshadow- are configured
Rule.description: The /etc/gshadow- file is used to store backup information about groups that is critical to the security of those accounts, such as the hashed password and other security information.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow- </xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Run the following command to set permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow-</xhtml:span> : </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # chown root:root /etc/gshadow- <xhtml:br></xhtml:br> # chmod 600 /etc/gshadow- </xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.10 Ensure no world writable files exist
Rule.description: Unix-based systems support variable settings to control access to files. World writable files are the least secure. See the chmod(2) man page for more information.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Data in world-writable files can be modified and compromised by any user on the system. World writable files may also indicate an incorrectly written script or program that could potentially be the cause of a larger compromise to the system's integrity.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Removing write access for the "other" category ( <xhtml:span class="inline_block"> chmod o-w <xhtml:em><filename></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:em>)</xhtml:em> is advisable, but always consult relevant vendor documentation to avoid breaking any application dependencies on a given file. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.11 Ensure no unowned files or directories exist
Rule.description: Sometimes when administrators delete users from the password file they neglect to remove all files owned by those users from the system.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">A new user who is assigned the deleted user's user ID or group ID may then end up "owning" these files, and thus have more access on the system than was intended.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Locate files that are owned by users or groups not listed in the system configuration files, and reset the ownership of these files to some active user on the system as appropriate.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.12 Ensure no ungrouped files or directories exist
Rule.description: Sometimes when administrators delete users or groups from the system they neglect to remove all files owned by those users or groups.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">A new user who is assigned the deleted user's user ID or group ID may then end up "owning" these files, and thus have more access on the system than was intended.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Locate files that are owned by users or groups not listed in the system configuration files, and reset the ownership of these files to some active user on the system as appropriate.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.13 Audit SUID executables
Rule.description: The owner of a file can set the file's permissions to run with the owner's or group's permissions, even if the user running the program is not the owner or a member of the group. The most common reason for a SUID program is to enable users to perform functions (such as changing their password) that require root privileges.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">There are valid reasons for SUID programs, but it is important to identify and review such programs to ensure they are legitimate.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Ensure that no rogue SUID programs have been introduced into the system. Review the files returned by the action in the Audit section and confirm the integrity of these binaries.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.1.14 Audit SGID executables
Rule.description: The owner of a file can set the file's permissions to run with the owner's or group's permissions, even if the user running the program is not the owner or a member of the group. The most common reason for a SGID program is to enable users to perform functions (such as changing their password) that require root privileges.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">There are valid reasons for SGID programs, but it is important to identify and review such programs to ensure they are legitimate. Review the files returned by the action in the audit section and check to see if system binaries have a different md5 checksum than what from the package. This is an indication that the binary may have been replaced.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Ensure that no rogue SGID programs have been introduced into the system. Review the files returned by the action in the Audit section and confirm the integrity of these binaries.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Group.title: 6.2. User and Group Settings
Group.description: This section provides guidance on securing aspects of the users and groups.

Rule.title: 6.2.1 Ensure password fields are not empty
Rule.description: An account with an empty password field means that anybody may log in as that user without providing a password.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">All accounts must have passwords or be locked to prevent the account from being used by an unauthorized user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> If any accounts in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow </xhtml:span> file do not have a password, run the following command to lock the account until it can be determined why it does not have a password: </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"> # passwd -l <xhtml:em><username></xhtml:em>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Also, check to see if the account is logged in and investigate what it is being used for to determine if it needs to be forced off.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.2 Ensure no legacy "+" entries exist in /etc/passwd
Rule.description: The character + in various files used to be markers for systems to insert data from NIS maps at a certain point in a system configuration file. These entries are no longer required on most systems, but may exist in files that have been imported from other platforms.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">These entries may provide an avenue for attackers to gain privileged access on the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> Remove any legacy '+' entries from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> if they exist. </xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.3 Ensure no legacy "+" entries exist in /etc/shadow
Rule.description: The character + in various files used to be markers for systems to insert data from NIS maps at a certain point in a system configuration file. These entries are no longer required on most systems, but may exist in files that have been imported from other platforms.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">These entries may provide an avenue for attackers to gain privileged access on the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:span>Remove any legacy '+' entries from </xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span> if they exist.</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.4 Ensure no legacy "+" entries exist in /etc/group
Rule.description: The character + in various files used to be markers for systems to insert data from NIS maps at a certain point in a system configuration file. These entries are no longer required on most systems, but may exist in files that have been imported from other platforms.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">These entries may provide an avenue for attackers to gain privileged access on the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:span>Remove any legacy '+' entries from </xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:span> if they exist.</xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.5 Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
Rule.description: Any account with UID 0 has superuser privileges on the system.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> This access must be limited to only the default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root </xhtml:span> account and only from the system console. Administrative access must be through an unprivileged account using an approved mechanism as noted in Item 5.6 Ensure access to the su command is restricted. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:span> Remove any users other than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> with UID <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> or assign them a new UID if appropriate. </xhtml:span>
</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.6 Ensure root PATH Integrity
Rule.description: The root user can execute any command on the system and could be fooled into executing programs unintentionally if the PATH is not set correctly.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"> Including the current working directory (.) or other writable directory in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> 's executable path makes it likely that an attacker can gain superuser access by forcing an administrator operating as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root </xhtml:span> to execute a Trojan horse program. </xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Correct or justify any items discovered in the Audit step.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.7 Ensure all users' home directories exist
Rule.description: Users can be defined in /etc/passwd without a home directory or with a home directory that does not actually exist.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">If the user's home directory does not exist or is unassigned, the user will be placed in "/" and will not be able to write any files or have local environment variables set.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If any users' home directories do not exist, create them and make sure the respective user owns the directory. Users without an assigned home directory should be removed or assigned a home directory as appropriate.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.8 Ensure users' home directories permissions are 750 or more restrictive
Rule.description: While the system administrator can establish secure permissions for users' home directories, the users can easily override these.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Group or world-writable user home directories may enable malicious users to steal or modify other users' data or to gain another user's system privileges.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Making global modifications to user home directories without alerting the user community can result in unexpected outages and unhappy users. Therefore, it is recommended that a monitoring policy be established to report user file permissions and determine the action to be taken in accordance with site policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.9 Ensure users own their home directories
Rule.description: The user home directory is space defined for the particular user to set local environment variables and to store personal files.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Since the user is accountable for files stored in the user home directory, the user must be the owner of the directory.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Change the ownership of any home directories that are not owned by the defined user to the correct user.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.10 Ensure users' dot files are not group or world writable
Rule.description: While the system administrator can establish secure permissions for users' "dot" files, the users can easily override these.
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Group or world-writable user configuration files may enable malicious users to steal or modify other users' data or to gain another user's system privileges.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div xmlns="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xccdf="http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.2" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Making global modifications to users' files without alerting the user community can result in unexpected outages and unhappy users. Therefore, it is recommended that a monitoring policy be established to report user dot file permissions and determine the action to be taken in accordance with site policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p> </xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:div>

Rule.title: 6.2.11 Ensure no users have .forward files
Rule.description: The .forward file specifies an email address to forward the user's mail to.
